entities.evidence: The verse names Enosh as Kenan’s father, matching Seth’s son in the Genesis genealogy.
The verse names Kenan as the son Enosh fathered at age ninety.

glosses.gloss: Marks Kenan as the direct object (untranslated).

analysis.evidence: אֱנוֹשׁ is the subject of וַיְחִי. The phrase תִּשְׁעִים שָׁנָה gives the duration Enosh lived before he fathered Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
analysis.sense: live for a specified span of time

analysis.evidence: אֱנוֹשׁ is the subject of both וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד. The verse names Enosh as the man who lived ninety years and fathered Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: תִּשְׁעִים שָׁנָה means “ninety years” and gives Enosh’s age when he fathered Kenan.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute

analysis.evidence: תִּשְׁעִים שָׁנָה means “ninety years.” With וַיְחִי אֱנוֹשׁ (“Enosh lived”), the phrase gives Enosh’s age when he fathered Kenan.
Enosh remains the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד, and אֶת marks Kenan as its direct object. The verse records that Enosh fathered Kenan at age ninety.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת קֵינָן, “he fathered Kenan,” אֶת marks the personal name קֵינָן as the direct object of וַיּוֹלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.
